item.title: PM Shehbaz says Makkah defence pact has sent 'message of peace, unity throughout region'
item.description:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that the recent Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan had brought the three countries “closer together” and sent a message of “unity and peace throughout the region”.

​​​​​​​The three countries signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), PM Shehbaz made the remarks during a meeting with Saudi Minister for Environment, Water and Agriculture Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadley at the Prime Minister’s House in Islamabad.

In a statement, the PMO said the premier reaffirmed the “deep-rooted, fraternal ties” between the two countries and conveyed his regards for King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.

He underscored that as strategic partners, both Pakistan and the kingdom must now focus their energies towards “deepening economic and agriculture ties to translate their longstanding relationship into a stronger, mutually beneficial trade and investment partnership”.

PM Shehbaz also expressed satisfaction at the “constructive engagement” between the two sides, particularly with regard to the export of agricultural products by Pakistan to the kingdom, the statement said.

“Both sides also exchanged views on enhancing agricultural productivity in Pakistan, through the use of technology, research and development and more efficient use of water resources,” the statement added.

The premier also announced that a delegation of agricultural experts from Pakistan would soon visit Riyadh to carry forward these discussions “with a view to realise the full potential of this partnership”.

Meanwhile, the Saudi minister thanked PM Shehbaz for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation and reaffirmed the kingdom’s commitment to deepening cooperation with Pakistan across the agriculture, water and food security sectors, the statement concluded.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during a summit at Al-Safa Palace.

The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

Pakistan has said that the pact is “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

On Thursday, Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman said the country would consider joining the pact “positively” if invited by the founding members.

item.title: Bangladesh to 'positively' consider joining Makkah pact if invited: foreign minister
item.description:
Bangladesh would consider joining the Makkah Pact “positively” if invited by founding members, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman told parliament on Thursday.

“Joining the pact or not has not come yet, as it is subjected to the intention of the parties involved in the pact. If they invite Bangladesh to join, then we will definitely consider it positively,” the foreign minister said, assuring parliament that Dhaka would assess the potential benefits before making any decision to join.

“More importantly, we have to keep in mind that it [the Makkah Pact] is the Muslim world’s self-defence mechanism,” he added. “And this is our family’s, the Muslim family’s, internal matter. So, there is nothing for others to be concerned about.”

Separately, opposition leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-i-Islami Ameer (chief) Shafiqur Rahman said on Thursday that joining the Makkah Pact was Bangladesh’s “own decision.”

“If Bangladesh takes a decision in the interests and needs of the country and nation, no one else needs to worry about it,” he said in a statement on Facebook.

Earlier this week, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said Dhaka had expressed interest in joining the pact.

“If there is one [agreement] in West Asia, if there is a security agreement between Islamic countries, then it is not unusual to go there. Let’s see. The matter is being viewed positively,” said Kabir.

​​​​​​​Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during the summit at Al-Safa Palace.

The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

The pact has been welcomed by the United States, Bahrain and Somalia, with Turkiye expecting Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”.

item.title: Claims that CDF Munir visited Iran as envoy for US 'incorrect, misleading': FO
item.description:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday termed claims that Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Iran as an “envoy” of the United States “misleading and factually incorrect”.

The army chief met the Iranian leadership during his day-long visit to Tehran on August 24, undertaken as part of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to end the stalemate in the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had also accompanied him.

Addressing a weekly press briefing in Islamabad on Thursday, FO Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi noted that the discussions held during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran “focused on regional de-escalation, breaking the military stalemate and exploring a negotiated settlement to restore peace and stability”.

“I will also highlight that claims by certain quarters that the COAS and CDF visited Iran as envoy of President Trump or the US are misleading and factually incorrect, as his visit was undertaken purely in the context and backdrop of Pakistan’s role as a mediator,” he said.

Andrabi asserted that the visit underscored Islamabad’s “sincere and constructive role in bridging the difference between Washington and Tehran”. He noted that the Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s efforts towards de-escalation and peaceful resolution of the conflict.

He stressed that Pakistan “remains engaged alongside our brotherly countries in sincere and concerted efforts towards resolving the crises in the Middle East and Gulf and with respect to the standoff between the US and Iran”.

“Pakistan will continue to actively pursue diplomatic engagement and support all sincere efforts aimed at reviving the peace talks and achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting resolution of the conflict,” he said.

Asked for a comment on the recent US plans for expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with Iran, Andrabi said Pakistan was “following international law and our bilateral trade agreements with Iran”.

“As such, our trade remains in consonance with our obligations,” he affirmed.

Asked about the US’s “economic war” against Iran, Andrabi expressed Islamabad’s hope that “all economic issues will also be settled in the long run” as part of a wider settlement of the US-Iran standoff.

Besides the CDF’s visit, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also remained engaged with his counterparts on regional developments, Andrabi pointed out. He added that over the past two weeks, Dar spoke with Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan three times.

A Pakistan-mediated memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the US and Iran in mid-June provided for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and left it up to Tehran and Muscat “to define the future administration and maritime services” in the waterway, in discussion with Gulf states and in line with international law.

But the deal, which was supposed to pave the way for talks on permanently ending the war, has since fallen apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi visited Tehran on Tuesday, where he discussed a framework agreement that would establish a “temporary corridor” for shipping and a project to clear mines in the strait.

Although there has been no clear breakthrough yet, and fundamental differences persist between Iran and the US, the latest diplomatic activity has brought the political and technical dimensions of the dispute back into focus.

The Iranian position, nevertheless, remains conditional as it continues to regard the Islamabad MoU as the appropriate framework, but wants Washington to demonstrate through concrete action that it is prepared to honour its commitments.

‘Tangible actions’ needed from Kabul rather than mere assurances: FO

Responding to a query on Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani’s reported remarks on a proposed security mechanism, Andrabi said: “Pakistan notes the proposal by the interim Afghan government’s interior minister for a dedicated mechanism to address contentious issues.

“We remain open to state-level dialogue. However, the sustainability of any mechanism will depend on tangible actions rather than mere assurances.”

The FO spokesperson emphasised that for any dialogue to take place, the Afghan Taliban must ensure that Afghan soil is not used to perpetrate terrorism against Pakistan.

“Kabul must honour its international commitments, including those under the Doha framework and ensure that Afghan soil is not used by hostile proxies, particularly the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and the Baloch Liberation Army, against Pakistan,” he said.

Andrabi reiterated that Islamabad remained ready for “institutional coordination provided it results in tangible and verifiable counterterrorism measures and effective border management”.

Asked about rumours that Pakistan had informed China’s special envoy to Afghanistan that it did not desire to hold further negotiations, the FO official said he was not aware of “any such words exchanged between our side and the Chinese envoy”.

He also “categorically denied” the Afghan Taliban’s claim that linked Pakistan to recent developments in Afghanistan’s Badakhshan. He further denied that Pakistan was forming any committee regarding Afghanistan.

On Pakistan’s UN envoy calling Afghan Taliban proxies, Andrabi said: “When their activities are at the behest of a certain neighbouring country to promote terrorism in Pakistan, to promote terrorism by Fitnah Al Hind and Fitnah Al Khwarij, then, unfortunately, we will have to call them proxies, as in doing so, they are not acting in their own interest.”

He observed that “destabilising Pakistan or killing Pakistanis ought not to be the interest of the Afghan regime”.

In the past few years, Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

FO rejects former Indian defence chief’s claims regarding 2025 conflict

Replying to another question, the FO spokesperson rubbished claims made by India’s ex-defence chief, Anil Chauhan, that an Indian Harop drone accidentally struck Kirana Hills near Sargodha during the May 2025 conflict after running critically low on fuel.

“We categorically reject the self-contradictory and retrospective claims made by the former Indian chief of defence staff regarding Kirana Hills,” Andrabi maintained.

He asserted that during the conflict, “Pakistan’s layered air defence network effectively thwarted India’s military objectives, while Pakistan’s subsequent response under Operation Bunyanum Marsoos demonstrated our ability to impose cost across the conflict spectrum”.

“No strategic asset or sensitive infrastructure was compromised in Pakistan. Attempts to retrospectively recast these events through selective narrative or dramatised production cannot alter the verifiable operational record of May 2025,” he said.

The FO spokesperson said that history is “established by facts and evidence, not by Bollywood-style retrospective claims”.

“These post-facto punches, if I may call them, 16 or 17 months after the war would be better directed at their faces,” he added.

Regarding a question about the removal of the structures outside Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi, Andrabi said Islamabad has “launched a strong protest” and termed the act a violation of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

The FO spokesperson noted that Indian “authorities used heavy machinery to demolish sheds, benches, and a walkway adjacent to the consular section” of the High Commission. He added that the facility was used by those seeking consular assistance and visas.

He pointed out that Indian actions against Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi were initiated “without prior notice, and therefore cannot be equated with the actions here in Islamabad”.

“Any attempt to link this incident to Islamabad’s ongoing non-discriminatory anti-encroachment drive in the Diplomatic Enclave is misleading,” Andrabi stated, noting that a notification was given to the Indian side but it “failed to remove such structures”.

He stressed that the drive “targets unauthorised structures outside all diplomatic missions, not just India, in the Diplomatic Enclave”.

Asked about a US panel’s concerns over the visit of the chief of Hindu nationalist group Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), Andrabi refrained from commenting on his US trip.

However, he noted that RSS and “its affiliates and cadres have been fomenting anti-Muslim hatred in India”.

“We hope that organisations and individuals with a conscience in the US will take up these issues with the leader of the RSS if he is visiting the US. I have no particular comment to make on his US visit per se.”

Makkah pact an ‘evolving security architecture’

Asked about Bangladesh’s interest in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, the FO spokesperson said: “As an evolving security architecture, the MJDA remains open to countries who share their commitments to collective obligations and common security interests.”

The joint defence agreement signed on August 7 aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Andrabi stressed that the pact is a “defensive framework aimed at safeguarding peace and promoting regional stability”.

He added that any formal request by another country to join the pact will be considered in consultation with Riyadh and Ankara.

“The operationalisation of the MJDA, however, remains at an early stage,” he said.

item.title: PTI to hold rally in Karachi on Sept 6, KP CM Sohail Afridi to tour Sindh
item.description:
KARACHI: The PTI on Thursday announced that it would hold a public rally on Shahrah-i-Quaideen in Karachi on Sept 6, while Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is scheduled to begin a four-day visit to Sindh on Sept 3 along with the party’s central leadership.

Addressing a press conference in Karachi, PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh said Afridi and the party’s central leadership would enter Sindh on Sept 3. The delegation would receive a major welcome at Kamoon Shaheed at 11am before travelling to different cities across the province, he said.

“The delegation, led by CM Afridi, will travel from Jacobabad to Naushehro Feroze on Sept 4, proceed from Naushehro Feroze to Hyderabad on Sept 5 and reach Karachi on Sept 6,” he announced.

Sheikh added that large gatherings linked to the party’s street movement would also be held in different cities during the tour.

“A major rally will be held on Shahrah-i-Quaideen in Karachi on Sept 6,” Sheikh said, expressing hope that the authorities would grant permission for the event. “Even if permission is not granted, there will be a rally in Karachi,” he asserted.

He said Sept 6 was Defence Day and that the PTI would speak about the defence of Pakistan and the rights of its people.

Speaking at the same press conference, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the PTI would also observe Sept 27 as Democracy Day and protest for the release of party founder Imran Khan, and called on people to continue raising their voices for their rights.

“This is not a battle for one day; it is a question of the future of the entire nation,” he said.

Raja said the country’s poor had expressed themselves through their votes, but their mandate had been “stolen”. He claimed millions of Pakistanis had voted for Imran on Feb 8, 2024, in the hope of determining their future, but their mandate was subsequently denied.

He also claimed that PTI candidates had won 21 of the 22 National Assembly seats in Karachi, while seats won by the party in Lahore and elsewhere had also been “taken away”.

Referring to reports of electoral irregularities, he alleged that the elections were marred by “worst rigging” and that candidates rejected by voters were subsequently imposed on them.

PTI Secretary General Raja said Pakistan had effectively developed two separate systems — one for the rich and another for the poor — and that the deaths of 14 newborn babies at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) had exposed the failure of a system that did not adequately protect the disadvantaged.

Expressing grief over the infants’ deaths, Raja said the tragedy had raised serious questions about the state of public healthcare. “A committee comprising those responsible has been formed, but the question is: where is the country heading?” he said.

He warned that a tragedy of this nature could occur anywhere in the country. Referring to claims that “the system had failed”, he asked which system had actually failed. “We need to fix the system that supports the poor,” he said.

Raja also said around 25 million children in Pakistan were currently out of school and that the country was wasting their potential. “Poor children are not receiving the education they deserve,” he said, adding that Pakistan had developed a degree of social and educational segregation rarely seen elsewhere, including Bangladesh.

“Pims tragedy is another manifestation of this inequality, as wealthy families generally do not depend on basic health units while poor people have no alternative,” he said.

Raja claimed that around 40 per cent of children in the country were behind in mental development for their age, leaving them disadvantaged throughout their lives.

“Imran Khan’s message is about the poor. He talks about equal education and opportunities for children of the rich and poor,” he said.

The PTI leader also alleged that people who raised their voices were being picked up, while journalists who spoke the truth were being removed from their organisations. “Journalists who used to raise their voice for the truth are unemployed today,” he said.

He said democracy had never been allowed to fully flourish in Pakistan and questioned whether the creation of new provinces would resolve the country’s political problems. Islamabad, he noted, was a small city, yet its hospitals and education system were also facing serious difficulties.

Raja further said any decision to create new provinces or alter the existing provincial structure should be taken by the people through an assembly representing their genuine mandate. He called for strengthening the local government system and devolving powers to the grassroots.

“Everyone knows how the mayor was made in Karachi,” he said, adding that no system could function if people continued to be deprived of their electoral rights.

Raja also alleged that PTI’s votes had been “stolen” in Karachi’s local government elections.

He urged people to come out and make their voices heard, assuring them that the PTI leadership would remain at the forefront of the struggle. “If 250 million people come out of their homes and onto the streets, this system will collapse,” he said.

item.title: Bangladesh urges OIC states to fund Gambia’s Rohingya ICJ case
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday called upon the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) member states to contribute to the voluntary trust fund established to support The Gambia’s case before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) concerning the atrocities committed against Rohingyas by Myanmar.
He also urged them to strengthen international efforts for the safe, dignified and voluntary repatriation of the Rohingyas to Myanmar.
The state minister made the call while speaking at the 23rd OIC Extraordinary Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) in Jeddah.
In his statement, Kobir welcomed the newly elected Secretary General of the OIC, Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, and assured him of Bangladesh’s full support and cooperation throughout his tenure.
He underscored the OIC’s important role as the second-largest intergovernmental organisation in advancing the interests and wellbeing of the Muslim Ummah.
The state minister expressed appreciation for the contributions of the outgoing secretary general and hoped that the new secretary general will build upon the positive institutional developments achieved during the previous tenure.
Reiterating Bangladesh’s unequivocal support for the Palestinian cause, he reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to a just and lasting solution based on the two-state solution, with an independent and sovereign State of Palestine living alongside Israel in peace and security.
Kobir expressed gratitude to the OIC member states for their support for the election of Bangladesh’s foreign minister as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (PGA).

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: PM Tarique Rahman to visit Türkiye for COP summit
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit Türkiye to attend the upcoming COP summit to be held in November this year.
He disclosed the information during a meeting with Türkiye’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Musa Kulaklıkaya on the sidelines of the 23rd Extraordinary Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Jeddah.
During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on regional developments and expressed their readiness to work closely together on issues of mutual interest.
Discussing bilateral relations, they expressed satisfaction with the existing level of cooperation in different sectors, including economy and defence, and underscored their shared interest in further expanding engagement across a wide range of areas and elevating bilateral relations to new heights.

item.title: Dhaka offers help as Nepal reels from deadly floods
item.description:
Bangladesh has offered assistance to Nepal as devastating flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 362 people and left several hundred missing, prompting Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman to express solidarity with the disaster-hit country.
Prime Minister Tarique expressed deep shock over the loss of lives and conveyed condolences on behalf of the government and people of Bangladesh to Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah and the people of Nepal.
“We stand ready to extend any support that Nepal may need at this time of distress,” Tarique said in a condolence message.
The disaster struck the Nepal-Tibet border region on Wednesday, with flash floods and landslides devastating settlements and leaving a trail of destruction.
Aid workers said entire settlements had been “wiped out”, while footage from the affected border region showed a massive surge of debris sweeping away vehicles and infrastructure.
Foreign Minister Khalilur on Thursday followed up Bangladesh’s offer of assistance in a phone conversation with his Nepalese counterpart Shisir Khanal.
Terming the disaster a “terrible tragedy”, Khalilur conveyed Bangladesh’s condolences and said the country stood ready to provide whatever assistance Nepal might require.
He said no casualty involving a Bangladeshi national had been reported so far and sought the Nepalese government’s cooperation should any Bangladeshi be found among those affected.
Khalilur also conveyed Tarique’s personal condolence message to the Nepalese prime minister and reaffirmed Dhaka’s solidarity with Kathmandu.
The Nepalese foreign minister thanked Bangladesh for its support and said authorities were still assessing the full extent of the devastation.
Nepal would communicate any specific assistance it required from Bangladesh once the comprehensive damage assessment was completed, he said.

item.title: 30 ministers, state ministers, whips assigned to oversee law and order among other things in 64 districts
item.description:
The government has assigned 30 ministers, state ministers and whips of Parliament to oversee and coordinate overall government activities in all 64 districts, including maintaining law and order, combating corruption and drug abuse, and ensuring good governance, transparency and accountability.
The information was disclosed in a gazette notification signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani on Thursday.
The assignments will take immediate effect.
According to the notification, the government has expressed concern that development allocations in various districts had previously been misappropriated through widespread corruption, with part of the proceeds allegedly siphoned abroad and the rest used for activities involving drugs, social degradation and threats to public and state security.
Against this backdrop, the ministers, state ministers and whips have been given the responsibility of supervising and coordinating district-level activities related to law and order, corruption and drug control, good governance, transparency and accountability, as well as development and public welfare programs.
Under the distribution of responsibilities, Iqbal Hassan Mahmood has been assigned Rajshahi and Natore, while Dr Abu Zafar Md Zahid Hossain will oversee Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari and Panchagarh. Abdul Awal Mintoo has been given responsibility for Lakshmipur.
Nitai Roy Chowdhury will oversee Chuadanga, Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Habiganj; and Ariful Haque Choudhury, Moulvibazar.
Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee has been assigned Chittagong. M Rashiduzzaman Millat will oversee Sherpur, Mymensingh and Netrokona, while Asadul Habib Dulu will oversee Thakurgaon and Dinajpur.
Md Asaduzzaman has been assigned Khulna, Satkhira and Bagerhat, while Zakaria Taher will oversee Feni and Noakhali.
Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain will oversee Manikganj and Munshiganj, while Sa Ching Prue has been assigned Cox's Bazar.
Md Shariful Alam will oversee Tangail and Narsingdi; Shama Obaed Islam Madaripur and Shariatpur; and Aninda Islam Amit Meherpur, Kushtia and Jhenaidah.
Abdul Bari has been assigned Bogra and Chapainawabganj; Sultan Salauddin Tuku Dhaka; and Mir Mohammed Helal Uddi Khagrachhari, Bandarban and Rangamati. Habibur Rashid will oversee Gazipur and Narayanganj.
Md Razib Ahsan has been assigned Barguna, Patuakhali and Pirojpur; Mir Shahe Alam Rangpur, Gaibandha and Kurigram; and Farzana Sharmin Sirajganj and Pabna.
Shaikh Faridul Islam will oversee Jessore, Magura and Narail, while Yasser Khan Choudhury has been assigned Jamalpur and Kishoreganj.
Ahammad Sohel Monzoor will oversee Barishal, Bhola and Jhalakathi, Md Shamim Kaiser Joypurhat and Naogaon; and GK Gaus Sylhet and Sunamganj.
Mia Nuruddin Ahmed has been assigned Rajbari, Faridpur and Gopalganj, while ABM Ashraf Uddin will oversee Brahmanbaria, Comilla and Chandpur.
The notification said the assigned ministers, state ministers and whips will advise government offices on controlling drug abuse and illegal trafficking, preventing smuggling and curbing serious crimes to maintain and improve the overall law and order situation in their respective districts.
They will also supervise and provide guidance on implementation of the government's election manifesto, poverty alleviation, employment generation, social safety-net programmes and various development and public welfare initiatives.
If necessary, they may attend district-level meetings and provide advice on relevant issues, according to the notification.
It further said the assignments were made in accordance with the existing powers of the prime minister and the government and decisions of the Cabinet, without undermining the legal authority of local government institutions or other constitutional and statutory bodies.

item.title: Malaysia to reopen labour market soon, agrees to recruit 10,000 Bangladeshis at zero cost: Ministry
item.description:
Malaysia's labour market, which has remained closed to Bangladeshi workers over corruption, mismanagement, syndication and irregularities during the previous regime, is set to reopen soon through a transparent process, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment said today, Friday.

In a press release, the ministry said the issue received top priority through several ministerial-level meetings between Bangladesh and Malaysia.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also discussed it with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar during his first foreign visit.

Tarique Rahman, Anwar Ibrahim hold joint press conference after bilateral talks

Malaysia has agreed to recruit 10,000 Bangladeshi workers on a "zero-cost" basis at Bangladesh's request.

The first batch will be sent on special chartered flights through state-owned Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL), without airfare or other migration-related costs.

The ministry said Malaysia has directly selected 25 Bangladeshi recruiting agencies and allowed another 312 agencies to operate as associate recruitment agencies.

The agencies were screened by a high-level Malaysian joint committee comprising representatives of relevant ministries, the Anti-Corruption Commission and law enforcement agencies, with no involvement from the Bangladesh government, it said.

item.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 552 dead, over 1,400 missing
item.description:
Rescuers ploughed on with their search Friday for survivors of deadly floods and landslides that struck Nepal and Tibet, with the threat of new torrents complicating their gargantuan task.
Emergency teams have recovered 552 bodies after a tsunami-like wall of water and mud crashed down on Wednesday, burying homes, smashing bridges and sweeping away vehicles.
More than 1,400 people are missing, including trekkers in the Himalayas and scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.
The US Geological Survey said the disaster -- the deadliest for Nepal since a 2015 earthquake -- was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.
The deluge of ice and mud also caused huge pools of water to form, with one of these formations becoming a direct threat to emergency workers scouring the region for survivors.
Nepali police urged all rescuers to “immediately move to a safe location,” saying it had received information that “a water dam has burst again on the Tibetan side.”
Separately in Tibet, China had earlier Friday paused its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding, before later saying the threat had eased.
State broadcaster CCTV reported that a lake formed by immense piles of debris began overflowing toward where rescue teams were headed, but later said the water level of the pool was dropping so the “the risk is gradually decreasing.”
Rescue operations were therefore “proceeding in an orderly manner,” it added.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, who chaired a meeting on rescue efforts Friday, offered Beijing’s help to Nepal’s emergency operations.
“China is willing to actively assist Nepal in its rescue efforts and provide support and aid to the best of its ability,” Xi said in a condolence message to Nepal’s president, according to state broadcaster CCTV.
Emergency teams had been racing to retrieve survivors from affected zones, where the widespread devastation meant food and water supplies were running out.
The Nepali military had meanwhile located people trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to find a way in to extract the survivors.
“Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel,” army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but efforts were ongoing to rescue more than 100 people trapped in the same area.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Buddha Tamang told AFP he survived only because he was inside a tunnel at the dam where he worked when the flood struck.
“I survived as I was in the tunnel,” said Tamang, who was airlifted on Thursday after being marooned for more than 24 hours.
“The senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away,” he told AFP.
Survivors in a makeshift Nepali hospital endured an agonizing wait for news of their missing loved ones.
Kula Priya, whose eldest son is missing, said she had lost everything when the wave of mud and water swept in.
“I don’t care for wealth. I just want my son back. If any of you could rescue my son, please do it for me,” she told AFP.
Nepali police have reported a death toll of 477 people.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
There are 977 people, including 517 foreign tourists, who are out of contact in Nepal.
Indians make up the largest number of missing foreigners, while the United States said 90 of its citizens were out of contact.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and where the only sources of information are Chinese authorities -- officials say 558 people are missing and five died.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash on the Chinese side.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others towards the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging towards her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” she said, then scrambled up a hill.
Logadarrsiny Raman, 26, from Malaysia, said she lost contact on Wednesday morning with her parents, aunt and uncle, who were on a pilgrimage.
“I’m very anxious,” she told AFP. “My only hope is to hear back from them that they are safe.”

item.title: Iran says still open to diplomacy as war with US hits six months
item.description:
Iran left the door open to diplomacy on Friday, six months into a war with the United States that has upended the Middle East, but only if Washington abandons its pressure campaign.
“Putting diplomacy back on track isn’t impossible. It hinges on US understanding of one simple fact: pressure doesn’t work,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X on Friday.
Diplomatic efforts, spearheaded by mediators including Pakistan and Qatar, have tried for months to bring an end to the war started by the US and Israel in late February to no avail.
While a ceasefire was agreed in April and a memorandum of understanding towards a final peace deal was signed in June, no agreement has been forthcoming and Washington has since declared “economic warfare” against Tehran.
In the latest effort to reinvigorate diplomacy, Araghchi met his Qatari counterpart on Thursday in the Iranian capital to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, closed by the Islamic republic at the start of the war, at the tail end of a week of intense Iranian talks with Oman and Pakistan.
A US naval counter-blockade of Iranian ports is squeezing petrol supplies in Iran, amid a shortfall of domestic production, as the US ramps up pressure on its foe, declaring an “economic D-Day.”
The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement.
Tehran has for weeks been holding talks on the future of Hormuz with Muscat, whose territorial waters account for the other half of the strait, while insisting that Hormuz will remain closed so long as Washington has not fulfilled its commitments under the June memorandum, which calls for lifting the US counter-blockade and removing sanctions.
“The US should build trust, speak respectfully, acknowledge our rights, and uphold commitments,” Araghchi said.
Iranian lawmaker Esmail Kowsari reiterated to state television on Friday that if the memorandum was not implemented and the US “does not respect its commitments, not only will the Strait of Hormuz remain closed, but the United States must be ready for our offensive actions and we will seek them in the most distant places.”
While Washington now aims to crush Iran economically, Tehran has weathered decades of international sanctions and experts remain sceptical about how much more pressure the US can bring to bear.
Analysts say the US plan to isolate Iran would require unlikely cooperation from trading partner China, which has defended its cooperation with Tehran and vowed to safeguard its interests.
China remains able to buy Iranian crude, an important source of revenue for Tehran, via overland routes not reliant on the Strait of Hormuz.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said “no one is above the reach of US sanctions” when asked if Washington would target Chinese banks that do business with Iran, ahead of an expected September visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping to the US capital.

item.title: Ismail Ould elected new OIC secretary general
item.description:
Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed has been elected secretary general of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
The Mauritanian diplomat and former foreign minister took the oath of office, succeeding Hissein Brahim Taha, in the presence of foreign ministers from OIC member states.
Earlier, OIC member states elected him as the new secretary general of the Islamic body during the 23rd Extraordinary Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers, held at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah on Thursday.
In his address, the newly elected secretary general said his election was the greatest honour of his career and the highest distinction he had received after more than three decades of international, regional and national service.
He added that his pride in receiving the trust was unparalleled, as was his determination to live up to the expectations of the organization’s member states and prove through actions, not just words, that his selection as secretary general was justified.
For her part, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of the State of Palestine Dr Varsen Aghabekian Shahin thanked the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for inviting the meeting and for its steadfast support of the Palestinian cause.
She pointed to attacks by Israel, the occupying power, on countries in the region and said Israel had become emboldened to act against them because it had enjoyed impunity for decades.
The minister called on member states to take practical, political and legal measures to hold accountable those responsible for settler crimes and those who support and finance them.
She stressed that incursions, violations and attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Al-Quds (Jerusalem) and the Al-Aqsa Mosque constitute a direct threat to peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Bangladesh-China sign MoU to boost technical education, skills development
item.description:
Bangladesh and China have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish a training centre under the China-Bangladesh Vocational Education, Training and Research Centre, opening a new chapter in cooperation on technical education and skills development.
Prime Minister's Education and Primary and Mass Education Adviser and Chief Spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office Mahdi Amin said the partnership in education, technical training and skills development would take the diplomatic relations between the two countries to a new height.
He made the remarks at the China-Bangladesh Education Exchange Conference held at Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University on Friday morning local time.
The MoU was signed by Md Daud Miah, secretary of the Technical and Madrasa Education Division of Bangladesh's Education Ministry, and Prof Zheng Pengwu, vice president of Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University, on behalf of their respective sides.
Under the agreement, the two sides will cooperate in vocational training programs, bilingual educational materials, educational resources, vocational education research, industry-education integration, industrial training in Bangladesh, study visits to China, and specialized training programs for vocational education administrators.
The cooperation will also explore partnerships with Chinese-invested companies in Bangladesh to expand practical training opportunities.
Mahdi Amin said the cooperation should go beyond signing formal agreements and create employment and other opportunities for young people.
"Turning education into skills, skills into employment and employment into opportunities is our main objective," he said.
He said the MoU was not merely a document but a commitment to turn cooperation between the peoples of Bangladesh and China into practical opportunities.
Three major international education and research cooperation platforms were also formally unveiled at the conference.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon and Fan Honghui jointly inaugurated the China-Bangladesh Vocational Teacher Training Centre.
Mahdi Amin and Prof Pei Hongwei inaugurated the Bangladesh Vocational Education Research Centre at Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University.
Md Daud Mia and Prof Zheng Pengwu inaugurated the Bangladesh "Chinese Language + Skill Development" Cooperation Centre.
The initiatives are expected to create new opportunities for teacher training, practical training for students, industry links during final semesters, curriculum development, research cooperation, teacher and student exchanges, Chinese language and vocational education, industry-linked training and employment-oriented skills development in Bangladesh.
Mahdi Amin said Bangladesh remains committed to further strengthening the longstanding friendship between Bangladesh and China under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
He said the Prime Minister's engagement with Chinese President Xi Jinping reflected the joint commitment to building bilateral relations based on mutual respect, mutual benefit and a shared future.
He said classrooms and industries, as well as education and employment, must be connected so that young people learn not only for degrees but also for careers, innovation and the future.
Bangladesh and China sign an MoU to establish a vocational training centre at the China-Bangladesh Education Exchange Conference in Jiangxi, China on Friday, August 28, 2026. Photo: Courtesy
Mahdi Amin expressed hope that international-standard technical education, joint scholarships, teacher training and faculty exchanges would help connect young people with opportunities in the global economy.
Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon praised China's achievements in education, technology, technical training and industrial development.
He said Bangladesh was keen to learn from China's experience in building a modern, industry-linked vocational education system and apply practices relevant to the country's needs.
The minister said Bangladesh has a large and working-age young population, which is one of the country's major strengths.
With access to quality technical education, practical training and modern skills, he said, the young generation could become a highly skilled, productive and globally competitive workforce capable of contributing significantly to Bangladesh's future economic and industrial development.
He also stressed the importance of ensuring that students acquire both academic knowledge and practical skills before entering the workforce.
Senior Chinese participants included Fan Honghui, deputy director of the Jiangxi Provincial Department of Education; Wu Zuowen, director of the International Office; Prof Pei Hongwei, party secretary of Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University; and Prof Zheng Pengwu, vice president of the university.
Presidents and representatives of renowned Chinese educational institutions, teachers, researchers, students and leading industrial entrepreneurs also attended the conference.
Representatives of 19 internationally recognized Chinese universities and technical institutes participated in the event.
The conference, MoU and three newly established cooperation platforms are expected to serve as important steps toward long-term Bangladesh-China partnership in vocational education, skills development, research and industry-education integration.
At the invitation of the Chinese government, Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon and Prime Minister's Adviser and Chief Spokesperson of the Prime Minister's Office Mahdi Amin are visiting China on a three-day official trip to attend various programs and discussions on technical and vocational education.

item.title: Lebanon’s Hezbollah Finance Crackdown May Be Designed to Fail
item.description:
Lebanon’s campaign against Hezbollah’s finances may be designed to look tougher than it is. Under pressure from Washington and international regulators, Beirut has done enough to claim progress by tightening the regulated financial sector against Hezbollah-linked entities, but without seriously threatening Hezbollah’s parallel financial apparatus, which operates largely outside it. This raises the troubling possibility that Lebanon is not merely failing to impose meaningful pressure but deliberately choosing measures that stop short of actually harming, and therefore provoking, Hezbollah. Lebanese leaders have repeatedly warned that directly confronting the group risks renewed internal conflict. A serious assault on Hezbollah’s finances would strike at the resources sustaining its organization and could invite precisely that confrontation. If so, Beirut has found a politically useful middle ground: cosmetically satisfying foreign demands to preserve the domestic status quo.

Iran remains Hezbollah’s main external source of money. Secretary-General Naim Qassem has acknowledged Iranian funding for postwar relief and reconstruction. In November 2025, the U.S. Treasury said Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guard Corps-Quds Force, its foreign-operations arm, had transferred more than $1 billion to Hezbollah since the beginning of that year, mostly through money exchange companies. Iran and Hezbollah have also used gold to move funds. Qassem has acknowledged smaller contributions from the Iraqi state, Shiite religious authorities and shrines, Iran-aligned Shiite militias, and Iraqi citizens. The Houthis raised funds directly for Hezbollah in 2019 and later for its Lebanese support base. Hezbollah has used cryptocurrency too, though the scale remains unclear.

Hezbollah also generates revenue through ostensibly legitimate businesses and commercial networks that conceal the group’s involvement behind nominal owners. Treasury says a commercial network run by financier Alaa Hamieh diverted more than $100 million to Hezbollah since 2020, while Hamieh allegedly used his state investment post to steer millions toward Hezbollah-linked projects.

Hezbollah-controlled and affiliated entities then manage and move the money. Its Central Finance Unit controls income and spending, Bayt al-Mal serves as its treasury, and Al-Qard al-Hassan (AQAH) provides bank-like services and holds cash and gold. AQAH officials have used personal “shadow” accounts to disguise transactions and move more than $500 million through Lebanese banks. AQAH-backed Jood SARL converts gold into cash, while Hezbollah-linked money-service businesses like CTEX have supplied dollars to Hezbollah institutions and recruited sympathetic money changers. WaTaawanou, a crowdfunding charity officially outside Hezbollah’s formal hierarchy, raises donations for needy Lebanese but directs much of the resulting spending to Hezbollah-run or -linked hospitals and businesses. These funds support personnel, weapons procurement, social programs, compensation, housing, and post-war reconstruction.

Lebanese measures have so far done little to disrupt this diversified financial ecosystem. AQAH’s liquidity problems do not demonstrate otherwise because they predated Beirut’s principal financial restrictions. It began delaying compensation checks in January 2025 and froze them on June 23, after nearly $500 million had already been disbursed. The Lebanese Central Bank did not issue Circular 170 until July 14. That measure bars regulated financial institutions from dealing with AQAH and related sanctioned, unlicensed entities, but does not close AQAH or seize its assets.

AQAH therefore remains operational. It retained branches that survived Israeli strikes, while Treasury said in February 2026 that Hezbollah continued using the institution and that AQAH officials had created Jood to ease its liquidity pressure. The Interior Ministry later withheld AQAH’s annual 2026 certificate of good legal standing pending investigations, but left its underlying association registration intact. An-Nahar reported would require a Cabinet decision to revoke. But, on June 18, Justice Minister Adel Nassar said the government had not even placed the AQAH file on the Cabinet agenda. Stripping a core Hezbollah institution of its legal status would mark a far more direct confrontation with the group, one the government appears unlikely to invite amid the current standoff over Hezbollah’s disarmament.

Judicial action has likewise stopped short of disrupting AQAH’s operations. Nassar referred AQAH and Jood to the public prosecutor in June for investigation. Yet by July 21, An-Nahar reported that the case remained dormant. Prosecutors were waiting for the Central Bank to provide documents establishing financial violations but had not themselves requested them.

Lebanon’s Central Bank also issued Intermediate Circular 761 on May 4, 2026, effective June 30, requiring regulated nonbank financial institutions—including exchange houses, finance companies, specialized lenders, and electronic-payment providers—to identify customers and report cash transactions of $1,000 or more, while flagging repeated transactions apparently structured to evade the threshold. But those requirements can still be bypassed through unlicensed or informal hawala networks, where a sender pays a broker abroad and a partner in Lebanon pays the recipient locally, without the original money passing through a bank or regulated Lebanese institution.

Lebanon’s restrictions have therefore changed Hezbollah’s methods more than its access to money. After Beirut tightened airport controls, Iran reportedly shifted to more couriers carrying smaller amounts of cash or jewelry while moving hundreds of millions of dollars through Dubai. When Whish Money, a Lebanese transfer company, closed WaTaawanou’s donation account in October 2025, the charity directed donors to AQAH and other transfer firms. Hezbollah also reportedly planned a new AQAH branch in Tyre without signage. Treasury has meanwhile documented Hezbollah financiers transferring companies to relatives or associates and creating new entities amid sanctions pressure.

Many of the steps required for real financial pressure already overlap with obligations Lebanon accepted under its FATF action plan, including more terrorist-financing investigations and prosecutions, better identification of true owners, seizure of illicit cross-border currency and precious metals, and stronger targeted financial sanctions. Applied to Hezbollah, that means closing AQAH, prosecuting officials who move its money through personal accounts, shutting Jood and replacement companies, seizing Hezbollah-bound cash and gold, revoking the licenses of financial firms that facilitate the group, and cutting Hezbollah-linked businesses off from state contracts, licenses, and institutions. Claims that Lebanon has clamped down on Hezbollah’s finances, or gone as far as it reasonably can, should be judged against such outcomes—not regulations, administrative measures, or assurances of progress that do not produce measurable, real-world impact.

item.title: India says Ganga treaty issues to be discussed under JRC
item.description:
India has said issues relating to the Ganga Water Treaty between Bangladesh and India will be discussed under the framework of the bilateral Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) as Bangladesh awaits New Delhi’s response on the matter.
“Ganga Water Treaty was signed in 1996 for a period of 30 years and all water related issues, river related issues between India and Bangladesh are discussed as part of the agenda of the bilateral Joint Rivers Commission,” said Official Spokesperson at the Indian Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal.
Talking to reporters in New Delhi recently, Jaiswal said further meetings of the Joint Committee of the Ganga Water Treaty continue to be held at the technical level.
The government is determined to renegotiate the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty with India while preserving the rights of the Bangladeshi people.
Replying to a supplementary question from Bagerhat-4 lawmaker Md Abdul Aleem, Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman on Thursday said Bangladesh remains active in pursuing its fair share of water from common rivers.
He said a team has been formed to prepare a new agreement following the expiry of the Ganges Water-sharing Treaty, and the Indian authorities have been informed accordingly. “We are now waiting for their response.”
The Bangladesh-India Ganga/Ganges Water Treaty was signed in 1996 for a period of 30 years which is expiring in December this year.
Experts said the treaty needs to be “reviewed and reformed comprehensively” before going for a renewed treaty by engaging economists, urban planners, sociologists and environmentalists in the planning, as Dhaka shares the ‘risk’ of not sharing it appropriately.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur, while attending the ninth Indian Ocean Conference in Mauritius, said they would like to see that there is an arrangement and a new treaty, or a revised treaty, ensuring the essential needs of their people.
“These are common rivers, and we have common legacies here, common interests and, as I said, there's no other alternative but to seek a solution that is durable and will win public trust. And this will also be very important to lay the basis for the relationship over the next 25 to 50 years,” he told NDTV on the sidelines of the conference.
“I think it is very important for Bangladesh and India to renew the Ganges Treaty. But it has to be revised. The very simple reason is that the treaty was done almost three decades ago,” Prof Shahab Enam Khan, who is the Executive Director of Bangladesh Center for Indo-Pacific Affairs, told recently.
